transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-17
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~49 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Ari (Redwood SE), Elena (Silverpine Head of NLP), Marco (Platform), Priya (ML), Kevin (Security)
Links shared: short-list spreadsheet (link), bench config (link), security checklist (link)

[00:00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:00:05] Elena (Silverpine): Hi, Elena here.
[00:00:07] Marco: Marco here.
[00:00:08] Priya: Priya.
[00:00:09] Kevin: Kevin—security.
[00:00:12] Jonah (Redwood SE): Jonah here.
[00:00:15] Maya: Sweet. Today's goal: scope a 30-day POC to eval a few open models, identify success criteria, confirm workload sizing and bench plan, and hit a target start of Oct 1. Does that sound right?
[00:00:28] Elena: Yep, that's what we want. We need to be super explicit on quality — our bar is high for extraction accuracy on financial statements, also support for English and Spanish, and some Chinese for a subset.
[00:00:40] Priya: To add, latency matters for our live UI — p50 < 200ms ideally for short extracts, but for larger multi-turn flows we can accept higher. Cost is also a constraint; we have a monthly budget cap for the POC.
[00:00:55] Maya: Great, let's break that down. Jonah, can you run through the metrics we usually recommend for this type of workload?
[00:01:02] Jonah: Sure. For a POC like this we look at four buckets: quality (F1/ROUGE depending on task), latency (p50/p95), throughput (tokens/sec or requests/sec), and cost (per 1M tokens or per 1K requests). We'll also track failure rates and memory/KV cache behavior for longer contexts.
[00:01:20] Jonah: For extraction tasks we recommend an F1 target threshold to call it a win — here maybe 0.85 F1 on the anonymized test set, or a significant lift over your current baseline.
[00:01:31] Elena: 0.85 seems reasonable but we'll validate. Our internal baseline is around 0.78 on the informal set.
[00:01:36] Ari (Redwood SE): Important to note: open models vary a lot on entity extraction vs. free-form completion. We'll need to pick candidates that historically do well on structured extraction.
[00:01:47] [00:02:00] 
[00:02:02] Priya: On multilingual, how do open models compare? We need good Spanish and at least passable Simplified Chinese output.
[00:02:08] Jonah: There are a few tradeoffs. Some models that are quantized to 4-bit run faster but might degrade non-English quality. Models trained on multilingual corpora tend to preserve Spanish better; Chinese is hit or miss unless the model has explicit Chinese pretraining. We'll include a mix — a medium-sized multilingual model, and one larger model optimized for English but with decent Chinese fallback.
[00:02:28] Maya: OK, shortlist-wise — we're proposing to test three open variants: 1) A multilingual Llama-3-style fork at 13B (we'll call it M-13B for the doc), 2) a 70B open model quantized (Q-70B) that's strong on English completions, and 3) a compact 7B fine-tune candidate that is cheap for high QPS. We'll send the exact model names in the sheet.
[00:02:47] Elena: Good. Can you also include a hybrid plan — like host the bigger for nightly batch processing and smaller for live traffic? That's something we might want to trial.
[00:02:58] Jonah: Absolutely. We'll propose an architecture for canary routing: live low-latency requests go to the 7B with prompt engineering and a reranker; heavy or fallback requests can route to Q-70B. The M-13B will be used for Spanish/Chinese-sensitive requests.
[00:03:12] [00:03:50] 
[00:03:51] Marco: On sizing — our expected POC traffic is about 20k requests/day with median request size 120 tokens and occasional batches that are 3–4k tokens for document-level extracts. Peak concurrency maybe 50–80 concurrent requests.
[00:04:05] Priya: For batch nightly runs, we might process 1.2M tokens in a job.
[00:04:09] Jonah: That helps. For 50–80 concurrency we recommend a dedicated small pool for the 7B to hit p50 under 200ms. We'll sketch the GPU sizing: a single A100-80GB or two 40GBs can serve multiple 7B workers with batching; the 70B quantized variant will need more capacity and is costlier. We'll include rough cost-per-day estimates in the sheet.
[00:04:30] Kevin: Security — what are the deployment options here? We need VPC/private deployment for compliance; SOC2 attestation is required. Also SSO, RBAC, and KMS for key management.
[00:04:41] Maya: Redwood Private meets VPC/on-prem needs. For the POC we can run in Redwood Dedicated or Private depending on your preference; Dedicated gives predictable capacity without full private control plane. SOC2 report, SSO/SAML, and KMS integrations are part of our enterprise package — we'll attach the checklist.
[00:04:57] Elena: For the pilot we prefer Dedicated with VPC peering if possible. We want to avoid heavy infra work but still keep network isolation.
[00:05:04] Ari: That's doable. We'll detail the network flows and what's needed for peering.
[00:05:08] [00:05:30] 
[00:05:31] Priya: Bench specifics — we want to measure p50/p95, tokens/sec, model cost, and quality against our gold labels. How do you run the bench?
[00:05:38] Jonah: We'll provide a bench harness (Python script + docker) that runs sample workloads measuring latencies with realistic batching, and outputs cost estimates using per-model profiles. We'll also run quality evals on your gold sets and return F1/EM metrics. The harness can be run in your env or by Redwood in a controlled bench.
[00:05:56] Maya: For transparency we'll share both the runner and the raw logs. You can re-run or we can run in Redwood infra. Which do you prefer?
[00:06:02] Elena: We prefer to run it in our environment for final validation, but initial passes run by Redwood are fine to narrow the list.
[00:06:08] Jonah: Great. We'll send the config for local run and an option to let us run if you'd rather.
[00:06:12] [00:06:40] 
[00:06:41] Marco: About timelines — we aim to start Oct 1, 30-day pilot. What's an aggressive but realistic onboarding window?
[00:06:48] Ari: Typical onboarding for Dedicated is 1–2 weeks for account and networking, plus a week for model selection and bench runs. For Oct 1 start we'd need sample data and signoff on models by Sept 24–25.
[00:07:01] Priya: Sept 24 is tight but doable. We'll prioritize the small anonymized datasets this week.
[00:07:05] Kevin: On compliance docs, Kevin will need the SOC2 and data processing addendum — send those ASAP.
[00:07:10] Maya: We'll attach SOC2, DPA, and the security checklist in the follow-up email.
[00:07:12] [00:07:40] 
[00:07:41] Elena: Back to model quality tradeoffs — can you clarify how prompt engineering or instruction tuning affects structured extraction? We've seen some models hallucinate entities.
[00:07:50] Jonah: Right — hallucination is a real issue with unconstrained completion. For extraction we recommend a structured output format and using a constrained decoder or a lightweight reranker. We'll also try synthetic fine-tuning on your gold labels or use LoRA to adapt the model; that reduces hallucination significantly. We'll include one quick LoRA baseline in the POC scope if you want.
[00:08:10] Priya: What's the expected improvement from LoRA?
[00:08:13] Jonah: Typically +5–10 F1 for extraction tasks with modest data (a few thousand annotated examples). But it depends on the base model. We'll show comparisons across the three candidates.
[00:08:22] [00:09:00] 
[00:09:02] Maya: Cost sensitivity — Priya mentioned budget cap. Can you share expected per-day costs across the three candidates so we can pick the likely combo?
[00:09:10] Jonah: We'll provide an estimate. Roughly: 7B cheap option maybe $40–80/day for your traffic; M-13B around $150–300/day depending on throughput; Q-70B could be $400–900/day given token volumes. We'll put exact per-1M token costs in the spreadsheet. These are examples and we'll refine once we nail batching and quantization choices.
[00:09:34] Elena: That helps. The hybrid plan (7B for live, larger for batch) might keep costs manageable.
[00:09:38] [00:10:00] 
[00:10:02] Kevin: Are there any known limitations around on-prem? We do have a constraint that models touching PII must not leave our VPC.
[00:10:08] Ari: For that requirement we can run Redwood Private in your environment or use Dedicated with strict egress rules and no logging of PII. We can also enable token-level redaction pre-request. We'll document options.
[00:10:20] Kevin: Ok fine.
[00:10:25] [00:11:00] 
[00:11:02] Priya: For the bench datasets — we'll send two: a small 500-doc set with gold labels, and a larger 25k doc set without labels for throughput. Anything else?
[00:11:12] Jonah: That's perfect. Also include a few long-context docs (10k tokens) so we can test KV cache behavior.
[00:11:17] Priya: Will do.
[00:11:20] Maya: Quick recap and decisions: 1) Test three model candidates (7B compact, M-13B multilingual, Q-70B high-quality). 2) Bench harness from Redwood; initial run by Redwood, final run by Silverpine. 3) Success criteria: target F1 ~0.85 or > baseline, p50<200ms for live flows, and cost within your cap. 4) Start pilot Oct 1, 30 days. Any objections?
[00:11:42] Elena: No objections.
[00:11:44] Marco: Sounds good.
[00:11:46] Kevin: No objections.
[00:11:50] [00:12:30] 
[00:12:31] Maya: Great. We'll send the shortlist and bench config by Sept 20, Jonah will follow up with the runner and cost spreadsheet. Priya you'll send datasets by Sept 22, Kevin will confirm security items by Sept 24.
[00:12:44] Priya: Got it.
[00:12:45] Elena: Thanks everyone.
[00:12:47] Maya: Thanks, talk to you next week.
[00:12:50] [00:48:30] 
Notes: occasional transcription artifacts — acronyms mis-heard (e.g., M-13B referred to verbally as 'm 13 bee' and sometimes transcribed differently). Speaker labels are mostly accurate but there are a few short segments labelled Speaker 1 where the recorder cut.
